findings.title: Silence menu item renders in the new list view but clicking it does nothing
findings.body: In the new ruler-less list view, RuleActionsButtons is rendered with only `promRule` (no `rule`/RulerRuleDTO). AlertRuleMenu computes `canSilence` from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(promRule, ...)`, which can be true, so the 'Silence notifications' menu item is shown and calls `handleSilence()` -> `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`. However, the drawer is only rendered behind the guard `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`, and `rule` is undefined in this context, so the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer never appears. The user clicks Silence and nothing happens — a visibly broken action in the primary new list view.

findings.title: Delete menu item can never render in the new list view despite prom-based delete ability
findings.body: The Delete menu item is guarded by `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}`. This PR adds prom-based ability checks (`canDelete` can now be true via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` even without a ruler rule), and RuleActionsButtons.V2's `handleDelete` only needs the identifier (`showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)`), but in the new list view `rulerRule` is always undefined, so the `rulerRule &&` guard permanently hides Delete. Users cannot delete Grafana rules from the new alert list view even with full permissions. The same pattern at line 123 (`canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`) also makes Pause unavailable in the list view.

findings.title: Refactor of useAllAlertRuleAbilities drops the federated rule group check, enabling edit/delete on federated Mimir groups
findings.body: Before this change, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and used it to disable Update/Delete/Pause/DeletePermanently for federated (cross-tenant Mimir) rule groups. The PR rewrites `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` to delegate to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false` (with a TODO). Since `useAlertRuleAbility`/`useAlertRuleAbilities` still route through `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` and are used by existing components (e.g. the old RulesTable / RuleActionsButtons), edit, delete and pause actions are now offered in the UI for federated rule groups where they were previously disabled. The backend may still reject the operation, but this is a UI-level permission regression.

findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered in rules.map without a key prop
findings.body: In the `rules.map(...)` switch in FilterViewResults, the 'grafana' branch now returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={...} groupIdentifier={...} ... />` with no `key` prop — the previous code passed `key={key}` (the comment in this file explains the artificial `key` exists specifically to prevent key duplication). The 'datasource' and default branches still pass `key={key}`. React will log a missing-key warning and, more importantly, reconciliation of this infinitely-appended list can match/grafana list items incorrectly when the list grows or re-renders.

findings.title: skipToken path computes Duplicate ability against Grafana permissions, wrongly enabling Duplicate for cloud rules
findings.body: When `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`/`useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` is called with `skipToken` (e.g. in AlertRuleMenu and RuleActionsButtons.V2 for cloud/Mimir rules, where `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)` is false), `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` still computes abilities: loading is false so `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported`, and `[AlertRuleAction.Duplicate] = toAbility(duplicateSupported=true, getRulesPermissions('grafana').create)`. AlertRuleMenu then ORs this with the ruler ability, so `canDuplicate` becomes true for a cloud rule whenever the user has the Grafana-internal rule create permission — even if they lack the external rule write permission that the ruler-based check requires. The Duplicate menu item appears and navigates to a clone flow that will fail.

findings.title: Prom-based abilities use alertingRule check for ModifyExport/Pause, dropping support for recording rules
findings.body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, ModifyExport, Pause and Restore use `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` as the supported flag, whereas the ruler-based equivalent uses `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` / `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule`, which matches both alerting and recording Grafana rules. In the new list view (promRule only, ruler abilities unavailable), Grafana recording rules therefore lose the Export menu item and pause support that they previously had. Modify-export and pausing are valid operations for Grafana-managed recording rules.

findings.title: Rule link no longer includes the returnTo parameter
findings.body: The deleted GrafanaRuleLoader's GrafanaRuleListItem built the view URL with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`, so navigating back from the rule detail view returned the user to the list. The new GrafanaRuleListItem (used by both GrafanaGroupLoader and FilterView) builds the href without `returnTo`, silently regressing the back-navigation behavior for the new list views.

findings.title: Component doc comment still says it loads from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints
findings.body: The JSDoc above GrafanaGroupLoader still reads 'Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints' and the `expectedRulesCount` comment still says 'Ruler response might contain different number of rules', but this PR removed the `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` call and all ruler handling from the component. The comments now describe behavior that no longer exists and will mislead future maintainers.

findings.title: Stale comment and variable name reference ruler rule preloading that was removed
findings.body: The comment 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX / Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded' and the variable name `cacheAndRulerPreload` remain, but the `alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)` dispatch they described was deleted in this PR. The remaining code only upserts the Prometheus groups cache, so the comment/identifier are now incorrect.
